ImageDescription.value:
Following her creative residency at Transcultures (Centre of digital and sound arts, Saint-Ghislain, Belgium) in October 2024, sound artist Joyul (Seoul-South Korea) presented an improvised performance centered around the daxophone (an instrument invented by German musician Hans Reichel—a wooden tongue mounted on a tripod with contact microphones, played with a bow and a dax, a curved piece of wood, one side of which is fretted) in the vibrant environment of the baroque Chapel of the Convent of Hautrage.
With the support of Transcultures & European Pepinieres of Création

165711339.title: File:Shattering Silence with Song How a 2018 Musical Theater Sparked Justice for Women in Rural Indonesia 01.webm

ObjectName.value: Shattering Silence with Song How a 2018 Musical Theater Sparked Justice for Women in Rural Indonesia 01

Categories.value: Musical theatre|Gender equality|Community art|Self-published work|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation

ImageDescription.value:
Shattering Silence with Song is a narrative-based musical theater performance held in March 2018 at Gedung Dewan Kesenian Cianjur, Indonesia. Initiated by the Bumi Manusia Foundation, the play merged traditional Sundanese performing arts with powerful narratives addressing gender-based violence. Drawing over 1,600 attendees, the performance served as a catalyst for dialogue, empathy, and advocacy on women's rights in rural communities.

This image is part of a broader documentation effort to highlight the transformative power of community-based cultural action in promoting gender justice. The initiative is also the subject of an impact report that details the program’s design, execution, and long-term outcomes in alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 5, SDG 16, SDG 17).

DOI: 10.5281/ZENODO.15477686

URL https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.15477686
